name: Separation of Powers
definition: An organizational principle of constitutional governance dividing state authority into three distinct branches—legislative, executive, and judicial—to prevent the concentration and abuse of power.
mechanisms: Legislative Branch: Enacts and debates statutory laws
Executive Branch: Implements, administers, and enforces laws
Judicial Branch: Interprets laws and arbitrates legal disputes according to constitutional standards
purpose: Prevents autocratic concentration of power by ensuring each branch functions with institutional autonomy while checking the others.

name: Rule of Law
definition: A fundamental legal principle whereby all individuals, institutions, and entities—public and private, including the state itself—are accountable to laws that are publicly promulgated, equally enforced, and independently adjudicated.
core_tenets: Supremacy of statutory and constitutional law over arbitrary administrative fiat
Equality before the law without privilege or discrimination
Predictability, stability, and transparency of legal procedures
Access to an independent and impartial judiciary
purpose: Safeguards against tyranny and arbitrary authoritarian exercise of government power.

name: Judicial Review
origin: Marbury v. Madison (1803, Chief Justice John Marshall)
definition: The power of a court to adjudicate the constitutionality of legislative statutes, executive actions, or administrative rules, invalidating those that conflict with a higher constitutional norm.
core_tenets: The Constitution is the supreme law of the land
The judiciary has the duty to interpret what the law is
Statutes repugnant to the Constitution are null and void
purpose: Serves as the ultimate institutional check by the judiciary against legislative overreach and executive transgressions.

name: Habeas Corpus
definition: A foundational common-law procedural writ safeguarding individual freedom against unlawful and indefinite state detention.
core_tenets: Demands that a detained individual be brought before a court of law
Requires the custodian to demonstrate valid legal authority and statutory cause for detention
Mandates immediate release if detention is found unlawful or arbitrary
purpose: Considered the bedrock procedural guarantee against unlawful imprisonment and executive detention without trial.
